title: Explanations for Whom?
paragraphs: Modern neural networks can classify images, translate text and predict the structure of proteins, yet the people who build them often cannot say why a particular output was produced. A model's knowledge is spread across millions or billions of numerical weights, few of which correspond neatly to a concept a human would recognise. This is what researchers mean when they call such systems opaque.

One popular response is the explanation produced after the fact. Saliency maps, for example, highlight the pixels that most influenced an image classifier's decision, and they look reassuringly like an answer. But in two thousand and eighteen, a group of researchers showed that some saliency methods produced almost the same maps even when the model's learned weights had been randomised. An explanation that barely changes when the model is scrambled may be describing the image rather than the model.

The computer scientist Cynthia Rudin has drawn a sharper conclusion. For high stakes decisions, such as those in criminal justice or healthcare, she argues that we should stop explaining black boxes and use models that are interpretable by design. Others reply that the point depends on the data: for raw images or speech, the most accurate systems remain stubbornly complex.

Both sides share an assumption worth examining: that an explanation is something a model either has or lacks. In practice, explanations are written for someone. A regulator, a doctor and a defendant may need quite different accounts of the same decision, and an account that satisfies the engineer may leave the person it concerns no wiser.

Interpretability, then, is less a property hidden inside the network than a relationship between a system and the people who must trust or contest it. Treating it that way does not make the technical problem easier. It does, however, make it harder to mistake a persuasive picture for an honest one.

options.text: Interpretability depends on who needs the explanation
options.explanation: Yazar yorumlanabilirliği ağın içindeki bir özellikten çok, insanlarla kurulan bir ilişki olarak görür.

options.text: Simple models should replace every complex system in use
options.explanation: Bu Rudin'in görüşünün aşırı genellemesidir; yazar iki tarafın da varsayımını sorgular.

options.text: Neural networks can never be understood by anyone
options.explanation: Yazar teknik sorunun zor olduğunu söyler, imkânsız olduğunu değil.

options.text: Saliency maps fully reveal how models reason
options.explanation: Metin bazı haritaların modeli değil görüntüyü betimleyebileceğini söyler.

questions.prompt: What did the 2018 researchers establish about some saliency methods?

options.text: Maps changed sharply once the learned weights were randomised
options.explanation: Tam tersi: haritalar neredeyse hiç değişmedi.

options.text: Maps were reliable for speech but not for raw images
options.explanation: Konuşma ve ham görüntü, açıklanabilirlik tartışmasında geçer; çalışmanın bulgusu bu değildir.

options.text: Maps were near-identical for trained and untrained models
options.explanation: Ağırlıklar rastgeleleştirilince bile haritalar neredeyse aynı kaldı; yani eğitilmiş ve eğitilmemiş model benzer harita verdi.

options.text: Maps were near-identical once the input images were randomised
options.explanation: Rastgeleleştirilen girdi görüntüleri değil, modelin öğrenilmiş ağırlıklarıdır; doğru olgu yanlış nesneye bağlanmış.
